SAA versus the cabin crews

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
SAA is in a financial death spiral. Now the cabin crew have blown the whistle and laid charges against members of the board and management citing R1.8 billion lost to corruption

Unique Selling Point:
Brilliant interviews with SAA cabin crew who have finally spoken out

Summary:
It’s no secret that SAA is in a financial death spiral. Now, to find the money to keep it afloat the finance minister is considering selling off the family silver- its shares in Telkom. It’s a crazy idea to fund the loss making SAA with the only SOE that is actually making money. Whatever he decides to do, Malusi Gigaba is running out of time. The airlines finances are about to crash and there is no money left in treasury for another big bail out.


Further information:
Banks have lost faith in the airline and last month, treasury had to find R2 billion rand in a hurry, when Standard Chartered Bank called in their loan. But R2 billion rand is a fraction of the money needed just to keep SAA afloat.

Think R44.5 billion rand, and that is close to the actual money needed to recapitalize the airline. And yet, all that would do is wipe out the past accumulated loss and debt. It would cover no debts for this financial year and the next, and neither would it provide any leeway to improve the fleet.

It’s against this background that SACCA – a union that represents 1300 of the SAA cabin crew, decided after 6 years to take a stand.

of telling their 1300 members that they couldn’t get an increase on their meal allowance – decided to make a stand. On the 26th April they went on strike. SAA says it was an unlawful and unprotected strike, SACCA disagree. Now SAA are seeking to recover damages of R35 million rand from the founding members of SACCA.

But this is not just a story about a strike. It’s about a lot more, because SACCA have blown the whistle on R1.8 billion worth of corruption at the airline, and they say management and the board are doing nothing about huge amounts of money that are disappearing down the hole. Christopher Shabangu is one of SACCA’S founding members and he has submitted an affidavit and laid charges at Germiston police station, against SAA management and its board for flouting the public finance management act. In response SAA, says SACCA has rolled out a campaign to victimize them. We currently await SAA’s response.

In a series of hard hitting interviews Derek Watts speaks to SACCA president Zazi Nsibanyoni- Anyiam, Gift Bilankulu, Christopher Shabangu, Firoz Kader and Mpho Moikangoa about their love for the airline, the forensic reports detailing huge corruption and how, after being ignored by the board, and two ministers of finance, in desperation to save their airline, they took the decision to take their fight to the media and the public protector

Press Release:


SAA
For years South African Airways has been facing financial troubles amid accusations of corruption and mismanagement at the national
carrier. It’s bankrupt and continues to lose millions every day, barely surviving on State-guaranteed loans. Now SAA’s own cabin crew union is
raising the red flag on corruption. Carte Blanche investigates yet another State enterprise in crisis.

Script:


SAA 2017 Final Script for TX SUNDAY 13TH AUGUST

Commentary One
Vuyani Jarana must be a man in need of a challenge, because he is about to leave Vodacom and take over as the new CEO of South African airways

Plane flies overhead up sound

And time is not on his side to turn around our technically bankrupt national carrier

LINK
They have been voted the best airline in Africa for the 14th consecutive year but that probably doesn’t refer to their financials. SAA have just had another major bailout and are losing millions every day

Commentary Two
SAA is paying its suppliers as it gets in money, but at the end of September, it must find another R6.9 billion rand to settle its outstanding debts. Interim CEO, Musa Zwane has been in the hot seat for 2 years and is keen to vacate it

Musa
At the moment – we are not publishing our financials because there are going concern issues that we are dealing with the shareholder at the moment

Commentary Three
The shareholder is the minister of Finance who represents you and I, the taxpayer

Derek to Musa
What are SAA losses we say about R370 million a month
Musa
Well it fluctuates Derek, but on average between R250 and R300 million would be in the ball park

Commentary Four
If SAA was listed on the JSE it would have closed down long ago says Editor of money web, Ryk Van Niekerk

Ryk
SAA has outstanding debt of just over R14 billion. The company also has R26 billion in accumulated losses, that’s excluding the R4.8 billion its projected to lose this coming financial year, so the total accumulated losses are north of R30 billion – add the outstanding debt of R14 billion you are close to R45 billion of outstanding liabilities – that is a lot of money

Commentary Five
SAA has now embarked on an urgent 5- year turnaround strategy based on three pillars stabilize the airline, defend their catchment area, and build new profitable routes

Plane takes off

But at the recent parliamentary meeting on SAA, finance minister Malusi Gigaba pointed out that SAA have had turnaround plans before.

Minister Gigaba
This is actually – the 2013 turnaround was not the first to be ditched. It was the 5th – it was the 8th and when we announced it in 2013 we were asked exactly the same question. What is new? how are you going to ensure that this doesn’t get ditched? and then it got ditched. So here we are with the 9th.

Commentary Six
They plan to cut routes, start by saving R900 million. They project profitability by 2020

Thandi Parliament
Why can’t SAA get it right? Why are people that are flying the same routes profitable, and we can’t?

Commentary seven
That is the question everyone from the finance minister to the cabin crew are asking. Mpho Moikangoa and Feroze Kader are founding members of SACCA, a non- political union formed to look after the interests of cabin crew

Feroze Kader
We fly 22 days of our lives and of those 22 days the aircrafts are 90% full. Where does this airline bleed its money?
Derek
There are calculations every flight on SAA sponsored by taxpayer to the tune of R500 rand?
Mpho
That can be true because we are feeding a monster and I can’t be doing my part and serve chicken and beef and be a safety officer. What is the CFO doing?!

Commentary eight
Well, the CFO has been trying to balance the books, but right now they don’t.

Phumezi Nantsi CFO up sound
For the 2017/2018 year end the company will post a loss of R2.8 billion, remember we are coming from a loss of R4.8 billion

Commentary nine
So, it looks like we will have to bail out SAA again, in September.

RYK
Since 1999 close to R40 billion in bailouts and guarantees were supplied to the SAA. Since 2008 the number is around R24 billion and this continues to pile up. I don’t think the government is capable of running a profitable airline and they have proven that over the last two decades

Commentary ten
But the minister remains convinced, privatizing SAA is not the way to go

Malusi Gigaba parliament
There will be no privatization at SAA. SAA will remain a state asset. It will be turned around it will come right

Commentary eleven
But fixing the finances of SAA isn’t the only task on the new CEO’s to do list.

In April, the cabin crew union ran out patience and went on strike over a meal allowance that hasn’t increased for six years. SAA contend the strike was illegal

Zazi
Enough is enough –and we are tired of talking. We have been talking, we have written letters now is time for action

Commentary twelve
Zazi Nsibanyoni-Mugambi is president of SACCA. Gift Bilankulu is treasurer.
They represent about 1300 cabin crew.

Zazi
We even said to SAA lets hang on, lets agree on something that we can pay later – we understand that you don’t have money, we have heard that story
Derek
Put the agreement in place?
Zazi
Put the agreement in place and say when you reached profitability…!
Derek
So, you willing to wait 20 -30 years?
Zazi
20 – 30 years no! and that is exactly why we spoke about corruption Derek, because something needs to give

LINK SAA
But this story is about much more than a meal allowance. It’s about the frustration that the cabin crew feel regarding the very management of the airline

Commentary thirteen
They say they have taken their concerns to two finance ministers and the board and got nowhere.



Zazi
it’s actually ridiculous what we have done! Knowing that there is a board meeting we went literally up and asked to see them for five minutes. We weren’t allowed to be seen. NOW WHERE DO WE GO FROM THERE? WHEN THE DOOR IS SHUT IN OUR FACES, ALL THE TIME

Commentary fourteen
Then in June, Christopher Shabangu, one of the founders of SACCA, was leaked extracts from EY, ENS, KPMG and the full audit reports prepared by open water. These are SAA’s own investigations into wrong doing at the airline

Derek
Christopher can you encapsulate what these reports allegedly reveal?
Christopher
They reveal a lot of corruption. Irregular expenditure of close to a billion rand

Commentary fifteen
SACCA believe SAA has been sitting on these reports and done nothing to stem the losses.

Zazi
When we set our eyes on reports that led SAA to the culprits of why we are losing money, then we thought no, no, no, no, no. There are gaps that need to be plugged here.

Commentary sixteen
SACCA has a point. EY flag a string of tenders in their report dated December 2015. TWENTY MONTHS LATER, the same tenders are flagged all over again in Open Water’s forensic report of May 2017. One of those is a component support tender which was eventually awarded to AAR for 125 million USD.

Derek
SACCA say you are ignoring the recommendations of your own investigations?
Musa
We are not, hence the board has pronounced on the steps to be taken to try and resolve the issue of the three reports that have been leaked.
Derek
SACCA is concerned about an apparently fraudulent contract of a billion rand, awarded to JM aviation in collaboration with AAR?
Musa
I am going to request again Derek that we allow the board to conclude and finalise its work.

Commentary Sixteen A
But AAR say they have provided SAA with much needed savings and they believe Open Water have tried to discredit their local partner JM aviation. They also say that the tender was challenged in the High court and dismissed with costs

Musa
If there is any wrong doing the board has promised that action will be taken regardless of who is involved

Commentary seventeen
And that could be Mr. Zwane himself. In a recent dispute between NUMSA and SAA technical, the Labour court ordered that the investigations currently underway at the airline, should include Musa Zwane and three other executives

Up sound Dudu
We did issue a statement as the board that we are not going to tolerate corruption

Commentary eighteen
Chairperson of the board Dudu Myeni is herself, facing a court challenge from OUTA for presiding over losses at SAA of R10.5 billion since 2012. They want her declared a delinquent director

Dudu Myeni
Those that are alleged to be doing wrong things there will be consequence management

Commentary nineteen
But SACCA are tired of delays and excuses, and on the 27th June, they announced they would be laying charges at the Germiston police station for SAA’s losses of around R1.8 billion rand

Christopher
We have opened a case against the board….
Derek
The entire board?
Christopher
The entire board! Against the CEO, the CFO We just followed the PFMA. Those people are responsible for the company. We aren’t saying they are the ones who took the money, we are simply saying they are the custodians at SAA

Musa
We haven’t seen anything from SAPS at the moment. The allegations made by SACCA will have to be tested/ and I think we need to allow that process to go on, but the board has started the process of ensuring that we bring all these investigations into a proper closure

Derek
It does seem quite a broad base though attacking the board and all the top execs from the CEO down?
Christopher
It has to be because we did everything humanly possible to try- probably wouldn’t even have opened a case if they had listened to us and said you know what guys we know about this. We are doing this this and that to deal with the situation

Commentary twenty
They have also asked the public protector to intervene


Zazi
We wish after we had written letters and had a press conference and written the letters, the board or management would have called us in and said OK SACCA, let’s work on this corruption. “WHAT DO YOU SAY YOU KNOW?” But that hasn’t happened

Commentary twenty- one
Instead SAA is claiming R35 million rand from SACCA for damages suffered during the strike

Gift
We are baffled by that because it is the first time in history that a company will sue a union for embarking on a protected strike

Commentary twenty -Two
But Zwane denies SAA are victimizing SACCA

ZAZI
Instead of acting on people who have done wrong we are now the ones being victimized and vilified, instead of the corruption being addressed! YOU ASK YOURSELF WHY!!!???

Commentary Twenty-Three
Vuyani Jarana has a solid reputation as a turnaround strategist and boy is he going to need those skills! Where to begin- when rooting out corruption, placating critical but unhappy staff, and finding R 6.9 billion rand, are his immediate priorities as soon as he lands at airways park

12 minutes.


PROMO ONE
Rooting out corruption, finding billions, and placating cabin crew must be top of SAA’s new CEO Vuyani Jarana’s to do list

PROMO TWO
SAA’s cabin crew union are tired of watching their airline decimated by corruption
Christopher
We have opened a case against the board….
Derek
The entire board?
Christopher
The entire board! We just followed the PFMA

PROMO THREE
Just how deep is the SAA’s financial pit?
Ryk
SAA has outstanding debt of just over R14 billion. The company also has R26 billion in accumulated losses

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): SAA is in a financial death spiral. Now the cabin crew have blown the whistle and laid charges against members of the board and management citing R1.8 billion lost to corruption
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Brilliant interviews with SAA cabin crew who have finally spoken out
metadata.Summary: It’s no secret that SAA is in a financial death spiral. Now, to find the money to keep it afloat the finance minister is considering selling off the family silver- its shares in Telkom. It’s a crazy idea to fund the loss making SAA with the only SOE that is actually making money. Whatever he decides to do, Malusi Gigaba is running out of time. The airlines finances are about to crash and there is no money left in treasury for another big bail out.
metadata.Further information: Banks have lost faith in the airline and last month, treasury had to find R2 billion rand in a hurry, when Standard Chartered Bank called in their loan. But R2 billion rand is a fraction of the money needed just to keep SAA afloat. Think R44.5 billion rand, and that is close to the actual money needed to recapitalize the airline. And yet, all that would do is wipe out the past accumulated loss and debt. It would cover no debts for this financial year and the next, and neither would it provide any leeway to improve the fleet. It’s against this background that SACCA – a union that represents 1300 of the SAA cabin crew, decided after 6 years to take a stand. of telling their 1300 members that they couldn’t get an increase on their meal allowance – decided to make a stand. On the 26th April they went on strike. SAA says it was an unlawful and unprotected strike, SACCA disagree. Now SAA are seeking to recover damages of R35 million rand from the founding members of SACCA. But this is not just a story about a strike. It’s about a lot more, because SACCA have blown the whistle on R1.8 billion worth of corruption at the airline, and they say management and the board are doing nothing about huge amounts of money that are disappearing down the hole. Christopher Shabangu is one of SACCA’S founding members and he has submitted an affidavit and laid charges at Germiston police station, against SAA management and its board for flouting the public finance management act. In response SAA, says SACCA has rolled out a campaign to victimize them. We currently await SAA’s response. In a series of hard hitting interviews Derek Watts speaks to SACCA president Zazi Nsibanyoni- Anyiam, Gift Bilankulu, Christopher Shabangu, Firoz Kader and Mpho Moikangoa about their love for the airline, the forensic reports detailing huge corruption and how, after being ignored by the board, and two ministers of finance, in desperation to save their airline, they took the decision to take their fight to the media and the public protector
